s1-release-core.deltaSummaryMarkdown: Regenerated the context for revision 11 and compared it with what I reviewed. Working tree: only .agentx/tasks/rayx-cli-versions/state.json is modified; rayx-man2.log and rayx-man3.log are now excluded via .git/info/exclude and no longer part of the inputs. Against the reviewed content: src/ is byte-identical to the release commit 40c3e13 (git diff shows no src change); the only product delta is the committed test `a_bad_release_name_is_refused_before_the_network_is_asked` in tests/self_update_release.rs (HEAD 1773373, +19 lines, already inspected: runs the binary with latest, 1.0.0-rc.1, 1.0 and >=1.0.0, asserts exit 1, `is not a release name`, example 1.0.1, empty stdout, no network), plus the release-commit version bump 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0 in Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock. Nothing else changed; finding s1-f1 stays resolved by that test.
s1-release-core.summaryMarkdown: Behaviour verified in source for all five criteria: release module is the single owner of parsing (semver, v prefix, no pre/build), ordering, installer URL (guest.rs now calls `installer_url_for`) and `MIN_REFRESH_RELEASE`; `exists` is a headers-only `curl --proto =https --tlsv1.2 -sfIL` through `Runner::query` (22 -> Missing, else Unknown). `run_release` checks existence, handles check/same, applies the receipt rule before any change, asks the downgrade question via `Refresher::confirm` (`--yes` skips, no terminal refuses with the `--yes` hint, no answer exits 1), installs via axoupdater `SpecificVersion` + `always_update(true)`, offers the refresh only on upgrades to >= 1.1.0, and persists nothing. The plain path is untouched (older Fake backends only gained `unreachable!` stubs). No password handling, no elevation, no new external program outside Runner (the installer run stays axoupdater, as before). Tests cover REL-1/REL-2/SU-2/SU-3 well and SU-1 including, after the repair, the early validation of the release name before the network (s1-f1 resolved by `a_bad_release_name_is_refused_before_the_network_is_asked`, which runs the binary and needs no network). Non-blocking notes: curl exit 22 is any HTTP >= 400, so a 403 or 5xx would read as `was not found` (per spec); after a downgrade to >= 1.1.0 nothing is printed about the refresh, which is the sensible reading of SU-3 (a `predates` line would be untrue). Source is unchanged since the first review; the only delta is the new test.

findings.descriptionMarkdown: Expected (SU-1, automated): `--release` accepts the REL-1 names and "is validated before the network is asked"; a bad value exits 1 with an example and nothing has run (epic constraint). Observed: the behaviour is correct in `update::run` (src/update.rs: `release::parse` runs before `GithubBackend::new`, error printed, exit 1) and the CLI wiring is correct (src/cli.rs `--release`, src/lib.rs dispatch), but `tests/self_update_release.rs` only drives `run_release` with an already parsed `Release`, and no test anywhere parses `self update --release <bad>` or runs `update::run` with a bad name. Removing the early validation or dropping `release` in the dispatch would pass every automated check; only the manual row 8 in docs/manual-verification.md covers it. Repair: add one test to `tests/self_update_release.rs` that runs the built binary (`env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_rayx")`, as tests/setup_update.rs does) with `self update --release latest` (and e.g. `1.0.0-rc.1`), asserting exit 1, stderr containing `is not a release name` and `1.0.1`, with no network needed; optionally also assert `--release 1.0.1 --check --yes` is refused by clap (--yes conflicts with --check) or that `--release` appears in `self update --help`.
